skill.name: cloudbase
skill.description: Guides CloudBase development, MCP setup, resource preparation, and deployment for web apps, WeChat mini programs, CloudRun, cloud functions, databases, auth, storage, and AI features.
skill.summary: Develop and deploy CloudBase apps with MCP-first guidance.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or automatic code execution was found. The static findings are Markdown backticks, reference URLs, a documented IDE config path, and scenario-routing words, so they were adjudicated as false positives. The skill still asks users to rely on CloudBase MCP and npm-based tooling, so package trust and CloudBase permissions should be reviewed before use.

remediation.issue: MCP setup examples use npm-based command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions where possible and tell users to review npm packages before running npx or mcporter commands.

remediation.issue: CloudBase management workflows can modify live cloud resources.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit approval guidance before MCP calls that create, update, deploy, or change billing-related resources.

remediation.issue: Some setup guidance depends on external documentation URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer versioned links or bundled fallback instructions for critical setup and deployment behavior.

content.value_statement: CloudBase projects often require coordinated auth, database, storage, function, hosting, and AI setup. This skill routes each task to the right workflow and MCP preparation steps.
actual_capabilities: Routes CloudBase tasks to scenario-specific skills such as auth, web, mini program, database, and AI workflows.
Explains MCP and mcporter setup, including schema inspection before CloudBase tool calls.
Guides resource preparation for auth providers, databases, storage, cloud functions, CloudRun, and hosting.
Defines deployment order for backend services, frontend apps, SPA routing, and README updates.
Provides CloudBase console entry points for common resources and management pages.
Adds engineering guardrails for TypeScript safety, runtime checks, and AI model configuration.
limitations: It is guidance only and depends on CloudBase MCP, user authentication, and project permissions.
It references sibling skills and external CloudBase documentation that may need live verification.
It does not replace CloudBase billing, quota, or console checks before deployment.
Command examples use external npm tooling and should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a CloudBase Web App
use_cases.description: Plan auth, database permissions, hosting, and deployment before writing frontend code.

use_cases.title: Deploy Cloud Functions or CloudRun
use_cases.description: Choose the correct backend target, prepare runtime settings, and publish with CloudBase MCP tools.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot CloudBase Resources
use_cases.description: Inspect environment binding, logs, resource status, and scenario routing before changing application code.

prompt_templates.title: Verify MCP Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me verify CloudBase MCP for this project. Check the expected setup path, required tools, and what I must confirm before any CloudBase action.

prompt_templates.title: Build Web Login
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a CloudBase web login feature. Identify the auth provider setup, publishable key checks, frontend steps, and verification tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Full Stack App
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the CloudBase deployment for this full stack app. Separate backend and frontend work, choose CloudRun or functions, and list MCP actions.

prompt_templates.title: Design AI Streaming Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CloudBase AI streaming implementation plan. Include eligibility checks, model routing, backend target, UI needs, and runtime verification.

output_examples.input: I need a CloudBase login page for a web dashboard.
output: Check provider status and publishable key before UI work.
Prepare auth settings through MCP, then implement the login interface.
Verify session handling and document the CloudBase resources used.

output_examples.input: Deploy my app to CloudBase with a backend API.
output: Confirm whether the backend belongs on Cloud Functions or CloudRun.
